## Cost-audit remediation plan (draft)

### Context

The `/cost` command exists (`api-cost.js`) but is nearly blind: **0 of ~10 Gemini call sites** feed it (`recordGeminiUsage`), **2 of ~25 Maps call sites** feed it (`recordMapsCall`), Routes API isn't tracked *or* even priced (`PRICES.maps` has no `routes` entry), and BestTime/Anthropic Claude/Alpha Vantage have no tracking of any kind. There's no per-user or per-day *spend* cap anywhere — only a *request-count* limiter (`rate-limit.js`), and it only covers 12 HTTP `/api/cuisine/*` endpoints, not a single Telegram bot command (`/s`, `/hidden`, `/eat`, technique taps).

One correction from my initial pass: I'd flagged `index.js`'s `skipCache = true` (search results never cache) as a "leak." Re-reading it directly showed it's a **deliberate v0.60.11 operator decision** — cached results were "clicking = same list, feels broken," reverted on purpose, documented trade-off (~$0.001/click). **Excluded from this plan** — not a bug.

One confirmed real bug: `cuisine-enrich.js`'s finalise loop deletes `v.reviews` (line 301) *before* `enrichSanctuaryRead` runs (line 310), so `vibe-summary.js:fetchReviewText` re-fetches the exact same `reviews` field from Google Places Details that was just discarded — a fully avoidable paid call, every search, every venue.

### Phase A — Instrumentation (wire the blind tracker)

Lowest risk, ships first. No behavior change, just visibility.

- **`api-cost.js`**: add a `routes` entry to `PRICES.maps` (Google Routes API `computeRouteMatrix`, per-element pricing — needs a quick pricing-page check at build time for the exact rate).
- Call `recordGeminiUsage(redis, model, response.usageMetadata)` after every real Gemini call currently missing it — `gemini-client.js`'s several functions, `translate-review.js`, `translate-name.js`, `name-gloss.js`, `durian-gemini-verifier.js`, `vibe-suggest.js`, the dish-extraction call in `cuisine-enrich.js`.
- Call `recordMapsCall(redis, endpoint)` at every Places/Routes call site currently missing it — `pipeline.js` (`searchText`/`searchNearby`), `hidden-verify.js`, `cuisine-venue-counts.js`, `transport.js`'s `searchNearby`, `vibe-summary.js`'s `fetchReviewText` (tag as `placeDetails`), `travel-times.js`'s matrix calls (tag as `routes`).
- Each call site gets exactly one new line adjacent to the existing API call — fire-and-forget, matches the file's own "must never fail the underlying call" contract already baked into `recordGeminiUsage`/`recordMapsCall`.

### Phase B — Fix the confirmed sanctuary redundant-fetch bug

`cuisine-enrich.js` lines 279-313: move `await ctx.enrichSanctuaryRead(top, ctx.csLang)` to run **before** the `delete v.reviews` loop (or before just that one `delete`), and change `vibe-summary.js:fetchReviewText` to accept the venue's already-fetched `v.reviews` array directly when present, falling back to its existing Places Details fetch only if absent (defensive — avoids a regression if some caller path doesn't have `v.reviews` populated). Removes one full Places Details call per venue per search, unconditionally.

### Phase C — Spend-based circuit breaker

Uses Phase A's now-accurate `getCostSummary` data. A small new module (e.g. `spend-guard.js`) that:
- Reads today's `getCostSummary(redis, 1)` total USD (Gemini + Maps combined) on a short-TTL in-memory cache (e.g. 60s) so it isn't a Redis round-trip on every request.
- Below a **soft threshold** (default $10/day, easy to override via env var): no-op.
- Above soft, below a **hard threshold** ($25/day default): log a warning, keep serving.
- Above hard: skip the *optional*, most-expensive enrichment steps only (sanctuary/Claude summary, footfall/BestTime, dish extraction) — never block core search/venue results — and surface a subtle "reduced enrichment" flag so the frontend can note it if desired.
- Applied at the same call sites Phase A instrumented, plus specifically gating `/hidden` (flagged as the single priciest, uncached, multi-attempt command).
- Thresholds are config, not hardcoded — you can tune them after seeing real Phase-A numbers for a few days.

### Phase D — Extend rate-limiting to Telegram bot commands

`rate-limit.js`'s `makeRateLimiter` is Express-shaped (`req/res/next`). Extract the core Redis-counter logic (bucket/incr/expire/cap-check) into a bare reusable function, e.g. `checkRateLimit(redis, { endpoint, chatId, cap, windowSec })` returning `{ limited, retryAfterSec }`, with `makeRateLimiter` becoming a thin Express wrapper around it (zero behavior change to the 12 existing HTTP call sites). Call the bare function at the top of the bot's `/hidden`, `/s`/free-text search, `/eat`, and technique-tap handlers in `index.js`, using the same `gia:rl:<endpoint>:<chatId>:<bucket>` key shape and fail-open-on-Redis-down semantics already established.

### Verification

- `node --check` on every changed file.
- Full `npm test -- --run` green; new coverage for Phase B's reordering (mutation-check: revert the fix, confirm a test goes red for "sanctuary must not see empty reviews") and Phase C's threshold logic (mutation-check: invert the comparison, confirm red).
- `gia-preflight` skill before any commit/PR touching `index.js`, `cuisine-enrich.js`, or the bot handlers (per this repo's own CLAUDE.md rule).
- Live confirmation of Phase A only possible post-deploy via `/cost` output before/after — flagged as a known gap I can't verify from this sandbox.
- Per repo convention: version bump + Journal entry + Register update per phase, and each phase ships as its own PR (Phase A is pure instrumentation / lowest risk — natural first PR).

## Gap Summary

Six surface areas lack full i18n support, creating a broken experience when users set `/language` to non-EN/FR codes (ID/RU/DE/ZH/JA/ES). The app currently promises 8 languages in the menu but delivers 2.

## Invariants & Assumptions

**I-1: Language follows user preference, not device locale.**
- The user's `/language` setting (stored in Redis) is the source of truth, not `ctx.from.language_code` or Telegram's client locale.
- Fallback chain: stored pref → Telegram locale (if available) → `en`.

**I-2: Admin commands remain EN-only by necessity.**
- `/cost`, `/ver`, `/oversight`, `/ftlog`, `/training`, `/v`, `/hidden` (admin) are owner-only and receive few enough calls that localization is lower priority than user-facing commands.
- **Exception:** `/log` is not owner-only; it gates by `isOwnerChat()` but non-owners see a silent no-op, so no localization needed.
- Decision: Admin paths stay EN; do not add ID/RU/DE/ZH/JA/ES to `/cost` response, `/ver` output, etc.

**I-3: User-facing command output must match the user's `/language` setting.**
- `/cuisine`, `/hidden`, `/location`, `/weather`, `/transport`, `/carpark`, `/buddy`, `/share`, `/recognised`, `/forgetme`, `/language`, `/privacy`, `/legal` — all must respect the stored pref.
- Fallback to `en` for any missing string key, not Telegram locale.

**I-4: Rate limits are user-facing and must localize.**
- `botRateLimited()` rejection message must read in the user's chosen language.
- Currently hard-coded EN/FR; expand to all 8.

**I-5: Enrichment errors are rare but must not crash silently.**
- Errors in venue rendering, review fetch, cuisine enrich, vibe-summary, sanctuary read, Places calls — if they surface a message to the user, it must localize.
- Fail-safe: if no localized string exists, fall back to EN, never to a key-name string like `error.places.unknown`.

**I-6: Venue-name, review-text, and Gemini responses are partially external and not fully localizable.**
- `local-name.js` pulls names from Google Places (English-primary, some transliteration).
- `translate-name.js`, `translate-review.js` exist but scope is unknown; assume they have their own logic.
- Gemini model in `/hidden` responds in the user's prompt language if requested; assume Gemini responses are NOT re-wrapped in i18n (cost + complexity).
- **Decision:** Do not localize external Gemini text or unstructured venue names; localize only *labels* around them ("Latest review ·", "Nearby carparks", etc.).

**I-7: Web surfaces (cuisine TMA, transport, oversight) have their own i18n instances.**
- `web/cuisine/src/v2/lib/i18n.js`, `web/transport/src/i18n.js` are separate and must sync with bot's SUPPORTED list and key naming.
- Assume they already localize their own UI; focus is on bot passing the user's lang pref to the TMA via `language_code` in the TMA context.

**I-8: No new strings; only localize existing EN/FR strings to the 6 new languages.**
- Do not add new keys or rewrite existing strings; only provide translations for keys that already have EN/FR.
- Assumption: 80% of existing EN/FR pairs have been considered for inclusion and are stable enough for 6-language rollout.
